sections.html: Barbus manipurensis was described scientifically only in 2000. Wild-collected fish reach a total length of only 3-4 cm. Its closest relatives are the Red Sunspot Barb (B. stoliczkanus) and the Odessa Barb (B. padamya). All the species mentioned can also be placed in the genus Puntius.
The fish originates from the Indian state of Manipur, after which it is named.

Males in breeding coloration are unmistakable thanks to a red stripe along the body, which also gave the fish its common name (jasper is an opaque variety of silica used as a gemstone, especially the red varieties). The sexes can also be distinguished by another, always visible feature: the iris of males is bright red, while that of females is yellowish.

Lexicon: Barbus: Latin, "the bearded one", referring to the barbels. Puntius: from the Bengal term "Punti" for such barbs. manipurensis: after the Indian state of Manipur. stoliczkanus: dedicated to the collector Ferdinand Stoliczka (1838-1874). padamya: the Burmese word for "ruby".

Its small size makes it an attractive alternative for aquarists with smaller tanks.
